stories.headline: BIG DROP IN WHEAT; PIT IN A TURMOIL; Break of 12 Cents a Bushel to New Season Low and 8-Cent Rally Mark Wild Trading. STOCKS TUMBLE IN CHICAGO Selling Swamps Exchange in 1,200,000-Share Day--Part of Big Losses Recovered. 1,220,000-Share Turnover. BIG DROP IN WHEAT; PIT IN A TURMOIL 15-Cent Break in Winnipeg.
stories.summary: Wheat prices plummeted and stocks tumbled in Chicago, causing significant losses for investors and speculators in the Midwest during a time of economic turmoil. The Chicago Board of Trade saw a massive turnover of over 1.2 million shares.

stories.headline: GALE AND RAIN LASH CITY; TIE UP SHIPPING; 3 KILLED; FLOODS THREATEN IN SOUTH; HIGH TIDE DAMAGES COAST Trees Uprooted by FiftyMile Wind--Streets AreFlooded Here.FERRY SERVICE HAMPEREDTraffic Is Slowed--Rising Temperature and Shift in WindPredicted for Today.WATERS RISE IN CAROLINAS1,500 Men Battle to ProtectAugusta, Ga.--SchoonersGround at Boston. Storm Covers Wide Area. Fishing Schooners Aground. GALE AND RAIN LASH THE CITY Aids Yonkers Water Supply. Damage on Jersey Shore. AUGUSTA FIGHTS OFF FLOOD. 1,500 Men Bolster Savannah Levee as River Approaches Peak. GALE HITS NEW ENGLAND. Two Schooners Are Driven Ashore in Boston Harbor by Storm. FLOOD MENACES READING. Riverfront Residents Move Out as Water Nears Danger Mark. THREE SHIPS STILL MISSING. Planes Search for Vessels Which Ran Into Florida Hurricane.
stories.summary: A severe gale and rainstorm hit the city, causing flooding, damage, and loss of life, with high tides and strong winds affecting the coast and disrupting shipping. The storm also threatened to flood areas in the South.

stories.headline: FARM DEBENTURE ADOPTED BY THE SENATE, 42 TO 34, AS RIDER ON TARIFF BILL; HOOVER FORCES LOSE AGAIN Export Bounty Scheme Has More Supporters Than Ever. MOTION DRAFTED BY NORRIS Makes Issuance of Certificates, Redeemable at 98 Per Cent, Optional With Farm Board. BILL NOW TO BE SPEEDED With Democratic-Progressive Coalition in Saddle, Accord Is Made for Longer Sessions. Hoover's Statement Against Plan. Debate on Rates at Hand. Action Rests With Farm Board. Seeks to Avert Speculation. Thomas for Mandatory Clause. For Duty on Long Staple Cotton. TEXT OF DEBENTURE RIDER. Duties of Farm Board and Treasury Prescribed in Norris Amendment. Provision for Applications. Receivable at Face Value. Debenture Rates Established. Penalties for Infractions. Guard Against Overproduction. CANADIANS EASY ON TARIFF. Milling in Bond Amendment Not Disturbing to Shippers.
stories.summary: The Senate adopted a farm debenture plan as part of the tariff bill, despite opposition from President Herbert Hoover, with the goal of supporting farmers and regulating exports. The plan allows for the issuance of certificates redeemable at 98 percent of their value.

stories.headline: EDISON RE-CREATES HIS ELECTRIC LAMP AS HOOVER LEADS IN TRIBUTE TO HIM; WORLD BY RADIO JOINS ANNIVERSARY FETE; OLD NOTE BOOK GUIDES HIM He Works With Aids of 50 Years Ago Till the Dramatic Moment. THEN DEARBORN IS ABLAZE Miracle Retold Round Earth Is Hailed by President at Dinner Honoring Inventor. DEBT OF MANKIND VOICED Young Speaks for Ford and Reads Messages From Prince of Wales and Hindenburg. Gratitude of All Mankind. Amid Scenes of 50 Years Ago. Nation Celebrates Edison's Feat in Golden Jubilee of Light Edison Re-enacts Experiment. Assistant Plays His Role. As One Master Workman to Another Homage of World-Wide Millions. Five Hundred Guests at Dinner.
stories.summary: Thomas Edison re-created his historic electric lamp experiment as part of a golden jubilee celebration, with President Herbert Hoover leading the tribute to the inventor. The event was broadcast worldwide via radio, with messages from notable figures like the Prince of Wales and Hindenburg.

rounds.blurb: The stock market crash occurred, causing significant losses for investors and speculators. Wheat prices plummeted and stocks tumbled in Chicago, with a massive turnover of over 1.2 million shares. A severe gale and rainstorm also hit the city, causing flooding and damage.

stories.headline: FAUBUS CONTINUES TALKS WITH HAYS; IMPASSE REMAINS; Little Rock School Guarded ----President to Meet Powell to Discuss Integration Hays Seeks a Formula U.S. Prepares Case FAUBUS CONTINUES TALKS WITH HAYS All Is Quiet at School
stories.summary: Orval Faubus continues talks with the US government as the Little Rock school integration crisis remains unresolved, with President Dwight D. Eisenhower set to meet with Adam Powell to discuss the issue. The US is preparing a case while Faubus urges the removal of the National Guard from the school.

stories.headline: Survey Finds Blow To G.O.P. in South; Survey Finds Little Rock Dispute a Setback to Republican Efforts to Win South NEGRO VOTE GAINS NEW SIGNIFICANCE Study Asserts Complications Face Democrats in '60 on Presidential Ticket G.O.P. Losses Reported State-wide Effect Noted Dilemma for Democrats Bias Laws a Factor North Carolina Maryland Missouri Alabama Louisiana Split in G.O.P. Ranks Texas Oklahoma Pennsylvania Michigan Illinois California Washington
stories.summary: A survey finds that the Little Rock dispute has hurt Republican efforts to win over the South, giving new significance to the Negro vote and creating complications for Democrats in future presidential elections. The crisis has caused a split in GOP ranks and highlighted bias laws as a factor.

stories.headline: BULGANIN WARNS TURKEY TO AVOID ATTACK ON SYRIA; Charges Troops Are Poised on Border to Carry Out Plan Directed by U.S. HINTS ACTION BY SOVIET Says Mideast Military Move Might Bring World War-- Washington Denies Plot Turkey Accused by Gromyko Bulganin Cites Geography BULGANIN WARNS TURKS ON SYRIA Bulganin Appeals to Turkey U.S. Disavows Any Role
stories.summary: Soviet Premier Bulganin warns Turkey to avoid attacking Syria, alleging that the US is planning military action against Syria with Turkey's involvement, and hints that such a move could lead to world war. The US denies any plot, while Bulganin appeals to Turkey and cites geography as a factor.

stories.headline: U.S. IS STILL COOL TO PLEAS TO JOIN BAGHDAD TREATY; But Is Expected to Weigh Turkey's Bid Again When Henderson Returns
stories.summary: The US remains cool to pleas from Turkey and Iraq to join the Baghdad Treaty, but is expected to reconsider Turkey's bid when Henderson returns. The decision comes amid concerns over Syria's drift to the left.

rounds.blurb: Orval Faubus continued talks with the US government as the Little Rock school integration crisis remained unresolved. The dispute hurt Republican efforts to win over the South, giving new significance to the Negro vote. Soviet Premier Bulganin warned Turkey to avoid attacking Syria.

stories.headline: 141 MEN AND GIRLS DIE IN WAIST FACTORY FIRE; TRAPPED HIGH UP IN WASHINGTON PLACE BUILDING; STREET STREWN WITH BODIES; PILES OF DEAD INSIDE; The Flames Spread with Deadly Rapidity Through Flimsy Material Used in the Factory.
stories.summary: A fire at a waist factory in a Washington Place building killed 141 men and girls, with the flames spreading rapidly through flimsy materials, during a time of growing industrialization in the United States. The cause of the fire is unknown.

stories.headline: 20,000 TROOPS AND TWO NAVAL DIVISIONS TO MOBILIZE NEAR MEXICAN BORDER; Fourth of United States Army Ordered to Concentrate in Texas and Southern California. REGIMENTS ALREADY MOVING Cruiser Division of Atlantic Fleet to Proceed to Gulf -- Pacific Fleet Held Ready. 2,000 MARINES ASSEMBLING Washington Explains It as Mobilization Test and Joint Army and Navy War Game. INTERVENTION TALK FOLLOWS Disorders in Mexico Have Caused Large British Interests to Claim Protection. FALSE RUMORS ABOUT DIAZ Washington and Mexican Authorities Deny That Aged President Is in Worse Health. GEN. CARTER HEADS FORCE Commanded in Philippines and Is Now Gen. Wood's Assistant as Chief of Staff.
stories.summary: The US is mobilizing 20,000 troops and two naval divisions near the Mexican border, with General Carter heading the force, as the country experiences tensions with Mexico, and President Taft's administration explains it as a mobilization test. British interests in Mexico are seeking protection due to disorders in the country.

stories.headline: SEEKS FRAUD NOTES IN CARNEGIE TRUST; Whitman Is Investigating Story That Names of Dead Men and Fictitious Persons Were Used.
stories.summary: An investigation is underway into alleged fraudulent notes in the Carnegie Trust, with Whitman probing the story that names of dead men and fictitious persons were used, during a period of increased scrutiny of financial institutions. Rollins is explaining his association with the company.

stories.headline: WON'T WITHDRAW, DECLARES SHEEHAN; Onus Is on the Party to Release His Supporters from Their Caucus Obligations, He Says. MUST RETIRE, IS OUTLOOK Murphy Said to Have Enough Votes for Cohalan -- Osborne Sees Trap for Insurgents in To-day's Caucus. WON'T WITHDRAW, DECLARES SHEEHAN
stories.summary: Sheehan refuses to withdraw from a political contest, stating that the onus is on the party to release his supporters from their caucus obligations, amidst a complex web of political alliances and rivalries, as figures like Murphy, Cohalan, and Osborne maneuver for power. Roosevelt is watching the situation unfold.

rounds.blurb: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire killed 141 workers, trapping them in a Washington Place building. The US also mobilized 20,000 troops near the Mexican border. Tensions with Mexico and financial investigations into the Carnegie Trust were ongoing.
